pairs: And the Pharisees and some of the scribes,
Et cum vidissent quosdam ex discipulis ejus communibus manibus,
And when they had seen certain ones from his disciples eating bread with common hands,
nisi crebro laverint manus, non manducant,
do not eat without repeatedly washing their hands,
holding to the tradition of the elders.
And when returning from the market,
And there are many other things which have been handed down to them to observe:
et interrogabant eum pharisæi et scribæ:
And so the Pharisees and the scribes questioned him:
Quare discipuli tui non ambulant juxta traditionem seniorum,
“Why do your disciples not walk according to the tradition of the elders,
but they eat bread with common hands?”
Bene prophetavit Isaias de vobis hypocritis,
“So well did Isaiah prophesy about you hypocrites,
just as it has been written:
‘This people honors me with their lips,
cor autem eorum longe est a me:
but their heart is far from me.
And in vain do they worship me,
For abandoning the commandment of God,
you hold to the tradition of men,
to the washing of pitchers and cups.
et alia similia his facitis multa.
And you do many other things similar to these.”
“You effectively nullify the precept of God,
so that you may observe your own tradition.
‘If a man will have said to his father
Corban (quod est donum) quodcumque ex me,
(which is a gift) whatever is from me will be to your benefit,’
et ultra non dimittitis eum quidquam facere patri suo,
then you do not release him to do anything for his father
rescindentes verbum Dei per traditionem vestram,
rescinding the word of God through your tradition,
And you do many other similar things in this way.”
And again, calling the crowd to him,
Nihil est extra hominem introiens in eum,
There is nothing from outside a man which,
by entering into him, is able to defile him.
sed quæ de homine procedunt illa sunt quæ communicant hominem.
But the things which proceed from a man, these are what pollute a man.
Et cum introisset in domum a turba,
And when he had entered into the house,
away from the crowd, his disciples questioned him about the parable.
Non intelligitis quia omne extrinsecus introiens in hominem,
Do you not understand that everything entering to a man from outside is not able to pollute him?
quia non intrat in cor ejus,
For it does not enter into his heart,
and it exits into the sewer,
he said “the things which go out from a man,
Ab intus enim de corde hominum malæ cogitationes procedunt,
For from within, from the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts,
Omnia hæc mala ab intus procedunt,
All these evils proceed from within
Et inde surgens abiit in fines Tyri
he went from there to the area of Tyre and Sidon.
he intended no one to know about it,
but he was not able to remain hidden.
Mulier enim statim ut audivit de eo,
For a woman whose daughter had an unclean spirit,
as soon as she heard about him,
and fell prostrate at his feet.
For the woman was a Gentile,
Et rogabat eum ut dæmonium ejiceret de filia ejus.
And she petitioned him, so that he would cast the demon from her daughter.
“First allow the sons to have their fill.
non est enim bonum sumere panem filiorum,
For it is not good to take away the bread of the sons
and throw it to the dogs.”
At illa respondit, et dixit illi:
But she responded by saying to him:
nam et catelli comedunt sub mensa de micis puerorum.
Yet the young dogs also eat, under the table, from the crumbs of the children.”
the demon has gone out of your daughter.”
And when she had gone to her house,
she found the girl lying on the bed;
and the demon had gone away.
Et iterum exiens de finibus Tyri,
And again, departing from the borders of Tyre,
venit per Sidonem ad mare Galilææ inter medios fines Decapoleos.
he went by way of Sidon to the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the area of the Ten Cities.
And they brought someone who was deaf
so that he would lay his hand upon him.
Et apprehendens eum de turba seorsum,
And taking him away from the crowd,
misit digitos suos in auriculas ejus:
he put his fingers into his ears;
Et statim apertæ sunt aures ejus,
And immediately his ears were opened,
et solutum est vinculum linguæ ejus,
and the impediment of his tongue was released,
Et præcepit illis ne cui dicerent.
And he instructed them not to tell anyone.
But as much as he instructed them,
so much more did they preach about it.
And so much more did they wonder,
He has caused both the deaf to hear
